Draw labelled gene arrows on stems at true genomic positions

Source: R/geom-gene-lollipop.R
geom_gene_lollipop.Rd

Fixed-size arrow heads make selected genes readable over large genomic ranges. Their stems retain the mapped genomic positions. Heads are packed above a shared baseline, in genomic order, using physical millimetres.

Usage

geom_gene_lollipop(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  stat = "identity",
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  headroom = 1,
  head_width_mm = NULL,
  head_height_mm = 4,
  padding_mm = 0.6,
  tip_mm = 1.8,
  gap_mm = 0.8,
  row_gap_mm = 0.8,
  stem_height_mm = 1.5,
  max_shift_mm = 25,
  max_rows = Inf,
  head_layout = c("compact", "columns"),
  anchor_tick_mm = 0.9,
  fan_height_mm = 2.5,
  lane_spacing_mm = 0.65,
  lane_clearance_mm = 0.5,
  stem_linewidth = 0.22,
  stem_halo_mm = 0.12,
  stem_halo_colour = "white",
  layout_callback = NULL,
  species = NULL,
  chr = NULL,
  subset = NULL,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = FALSE
)

GeomGeneLollipop

Format

An object of class GeomGeneLollipop (inherits from Geom, ggproto, gg) of length 12.

Arguments

mapping, data, stat, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard ggplot2 layer arguments. Map x, y, strand and optionally label. Columns named x, y, and strand are mapped automatically.

headroom

Positive y-data-unit space reserved above the baseline.

head_width_mm

Common physical head width. NULL fits the longest label across the entire layer without shrinking text.

head_height_mm

Minimum head height in millimetres; grows to fit text.

padding_mm

Padding around internal labels in millimetres.

tip_mm

Length of the triangular arrow tip in millimetres.

gap_mm

Horizontal clearance between heads in the same row.

row_gap_mm

Vertical clearance between rows of heads.

stem_height_mm

Clearance from the baseline to the first head row.

max_shift_mm

Maximum horizontal displacement from a true anchor.

max_rows

Maximum number of head rows, or Inf.

head_layout

"compact" retains ordered centres with interleaved rows. "columns" groups consecutive genes into columns read top to bottom, then left to right, and routes leaders beside the heads.

anchor_tick_mm

Height of exact-position vertical anchor ticks.

fan_height_mm

Height of the clear routing band above the ticks in column mode. stem_height_mm separates this band from the lowest heads.

lane_spacing_mm

Distance between leader lanes in each column gutter.

lane_clearance_mm

Clearance beside gutter lanes and head outlines.

stem_linewidth

Width of coloured leaders in millimetres. Their colour defaults to a darker shade of the head fill; map or set stem_colour to override it. Anchor ticks use at most 0.16 mm linewidth.

stem_halo_mm

Extra halo width on each side of a leader, drawn beneath all coloured leaders.

stem_halo_colour

Halo colour; defaults to white.

layout_callback

Optional function receiving a data frame of physical head and anchor coordinates at draw time, once per panel per draw. Units are millimetres relative to the panel's lower left corner. genomic_x retains the original untransformed genomic coordinate.

species, chr, subset

Optional Syn individual, chromosome and genomic window selectors.

Value

A ggplot layer.

Details

Use one shared y baseline per panel. The common width includes arrow-tip space so labels fit inside the arrow body. Missing labels remain unlabelled heads. Unknown strands produce rectangular heads. Reversing the x scale or coordinate reverses the arrows. Only linear Cartesian coordinates are supported. Heads outside a coordinate zoom are omitted with their anchors.

Heads are stylised gene symbols, not scaled transcript structures. For Syn-backed input the anchor is the midpoint of the complete gene span, including genes without coding transcripts. Retain native-scale context genes in a separate geom_gene() layer if needed.

Compact packing uses the smallest feasible number of round-robin rows with ordered head centres and bounded displacement. Automatic column packing uses the smallest feasible number of rows with one common x centre per group of consecutive genes. Read each column top to bottom, then the next column to its right. Map optional numeric head_row to keep matching genes in shared rows across facets. Rows are positive integers numbered bottom to top. Supply a row for every gene in the layer, and use head_layout = "columns". Fixed-row packing finds the smallest feasible number of ordered, contiguous columns while retaining every supplied row index. Unused slots stay blank; duplicated genes remain separate heads. Shared rows are supplied layout metadata, not inferred orthology or evidence of gene absence.

Leaders run through a clear band and ordered lanes to each head's left edge, avoiding the other heads. Both layouts are recomputed on the output device. If every head cannot fit the available width or headroom, drawing errors instead of dropping genes or reducing font size. Increase the output size, headroom or displacement allowance to resolve the error.

Examples

genes <- data.frame(x = c(1e6, 1.02e6, 2e6), y = 0,
                    strand = c("+", "-", "+"), label = c("A", "B*", "C"))
ggplot2::ggplot() + geom_gene_lollipop(data = genes) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 6e6))
